# Context Cost

> Essays and research on software design, context cost, and AI-assisted engineering.

Context Cost is written by Lianghui Zhang, who writes as Leric Zhang. The central research work is the CMP online series. It explores Context-Cost-Driven Software Design: a perspective that evaluates software structure by the cost of acquiring sufficient context for correct modification. The Context Minimization Principle (CMP) is its core principle. Depth, Breadth, and Context Transformation are analytical tools; boundaries, locality, architecture, testing, and language mechanisms are applications.

## Core contribution

CMP proposes a common evaluation criterion for software design trade-offs. Its argument runs from realistic modifications, through sufficient context for correctness, to the acquisition cost that design can transform. Traditional principles are candidate mechanisms whose benefits and costs can be compared; conforming to a named principle is not sufficient evidence of good design. A justified conclusion can favor separate implementations over a shared abstraction, or a direct call over an interface, when the realistic modification pattern makes the latter more expensive to understand and verify.

Reduce, Relocate, Index, and Check change acquisition work, not necessarily information volume. Depth and Breadth describe how costs grow; architecture routes acquisition. More types, tests, or documentation can improve a design even when token consumption rises. These are theoretical arguments and worked examples, not a universally calibrated metric or established empirical gains.

- [Core Thesis & Contributions](https://www.contextcost.dev/research/cmp/start/core-thesis-and-contributions/): five connected claims, contrasting design decisions, limitations, and reading-check questions.
- [核心主张与贡献（中文）](https://www.contextcost.dev/zh/research/cmp/start/core-thesis-and-contributions/)

## Canonical work

- [CMP — Context-Cost-Driven Software Design](https://www.contextcost.dev/cmp/): the evolving CMP online series.
- [CMP preprint (v1.0.1, DOI)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21331759): the fixed, citable PDF edition.
- [CMP research chapters](https://www.contextcost.dev/research/cmp/): individual chapters, with version and update metadata.
- [CMP print edition](https://www.contextcost.dev/cmp/print/): a noindex, printable compilation of published chapters.

## Citation and attribution

Retain "CMP" for the online book, its chapters, language editions, print edition, and RSS feed. Use "Context-Cost-Driven Software Design" for the broader design perspective and "Context Minimization Principle (CMP)" for its core principle. Attribute both to Lianghui Zhang (Leric Zhang). The fixed preprint retains its published title, "Context Minimization Principle".

Preferred citation:

> Lianghui Zhang. (2026). *Context Minimization Principle* (Version v1.0.1) [Preprint]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21331759

The CMP online book and research chapters are licensed under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The website source code, third-party assets, and non-CMP content are not covered by that license unless explicitly stated.
